title: Getting started with Wistudi
text: If someone has invited you to a lesson, start with their link. If you want to explore or publish, sign in and use Discover or your publishing workspace. Choose your starting point You do not need to build anything to take part in learning. Start with the task you came to do: Complete a lesson: open the link from your teacher, trainer or publisher. Follow the invitation and sign-in instructions on that page. Explore learning: open Discover to browse available XP Videos and Flows. Create learning: use the XP Videos or Flows area of your publishing workspace. Begin with one short lesson rather than a complete course. Attend an event: use the event's registration or joining link. Event registration and access to a separate lesson are different actions; follow the instructions supplied by your host. Create or access your account Open Create an account . If you already have an account, choose Sign In instead. For email registration, enter your first name, last name, email address and password, then choose Create Account . Use an email inbox you can access. Look for the verification email and follow its link. If it is missing, check spam or junk and use Resend verification email on the verification screen. Complete any profile or onboarding requirements shown in your account. If you arrived through an invitation, return to the original invitation link after signing in. Account creation does not give access to every private lesson, organisation or event. Access still depends on the invitation, account permissions and the content's availability. Understand XP Videos and Flows An XP Video adds activities and checkpoints to a video. A checkpoint can ask you to answer, reflect or complete a task while watching. A Flow brings pages, content and activities into a learning sequence. It can combine explanations, videos, questions and resources in one experience. If you are learning, follow the instructions and requirements displayed in the experience. If you are publishing, choose the format that fits the learning: video-led learning suits an XP Video; a sequence of mixed content suits a Flow. If part of the platform is locked Some navigation areas have onboarding requirements. Read the requirement shown beside the locked section and use its action to continue. Do not create another account to try to unlock it. A message that your account or content has restricted access needs a different response: return to your invitation, contact the person who shared the content, or ask Wistudi Support. See Dashboard and workspaces for help choosing the right area.

title: Your account and profile
text: Use your own account and an email address you can access. My Profile is for your profile; Account Settings is for account preferences. Review visibility before sharing a profile. Register with an email you control Open the registration page . Enter your first name, last name, email address and password in the fields shown. Review the information and choose Create Account . Open the verification email and follow the link to confirm your email address. Continue to sign in and complete the profile or onboarding steps shown. If you already have an account, use Sign In . Creating another account can leave invitations, learning and published work associated with different identities. Independent registration is for users aged 16 or over. Younger learners need an approved supervised arrangement. A parent, guardian or authorised organisation should contact Wistudi if they need help arranging access. Verify your email address Verification confirms that you can access the email address on your account. Check that the address displayed on the verification screen is correct, then look in your inbox and spam or junk folder. Use Resend verification email if needed. If a verification link is invalid or expired, choose Request a new link and use the newly issued email. Copying only part of the URL can prevent it from working. Never send your verification link or password to another person. Support may ask for your account email and the error message, but does not need your password. Find your profile and settings Open your account menu and look for My Profile or Account Settings . My Profile: view your profile and the editing options available to you. Review your display information before sharing your profile. Account Settings: manage the account preferences and settings available for your account. Profile setup: if onboarding asks you to complete your profile, follow that prompt. You can also open profile settings while signed in. After editing, use the save or confirmation control shown and check that the update succeeds before leaving. A setting labelled Coming soon is not a promise that the associated service is active. Understand visibility and protect your account Your public profile and your private account records are different. Profile information may be displayed according to your visibility and publishing settings; that does not make private learner progress, assessments or transactions public. Only include contact details or personal information you intend to share in a public profile. Review the Privacy Policy for how Wistudi handles personal information. Keep your password private, use a password you do not reuse elsewhere, and sign out on a shared device. If you no longer control the account email or suspect someone else has accessed your account, contact support@wistudi.com before creating a replacement account.

title: Sign-in and account recovery
text: Use the email address and sign-in method connected to your account. For a forgotten password, choose Forgot your password? and request a reset link. Sign in to the correct account Open Sign In . For email sign-in, enter your account email and password, then choose Sign In . If you registered using Google, use the Google sign-in option with the same Google account. Complete any verification or account prompts shown. If you are trying to open shared learning, return to the original invitation link after signing in. Check for typing mistakes and unwanted spaces in your email address. If you use more than one email or Google account, make sure you are using the identity that received the invitation or owns the work you need. Reset a forgotten password On the sign-in page, choose Forgot your password? , or open password recovery . Enter your account email address and choose Send Reset Link . Open the reset email and follow the complete link. Enter your new password in New Password and repeat it in Confirm New Password . Choose Reset Password . Once the success message appears, return to sign-in and use your new password. Follow the password requirements shown by the form. If the link is invalid, expired or missing its reset token, choose Request a new link and use the new email. Do not forward a reset link to anyone else. If an account email has not arrived Check that the email address you entered is correct and that you can receive mail in that inbox. Look in spam, junk and any filtered mail folders. Use Resend reset link or Resend verification email on the relevant screen. Open the message for the action you just requested. An email-verification link and a password-reset link have different purposes. If the message still does not arrive, contact support with your account email, the action you requested and the approximate time. Do not include your password or a full reset or verification link. If your account is restricted or suspended A password reset does not remove an account restriction. If Wistudi displays a suspension or access message, read the explanation and contact your organisation's administrator or Wistudi Support as appropriate. Include the exact message and the email address on your account. Avoid creating another account to bypass a restriction; it can separate your learning and content from the original account. If you cannot access the email inbox linked to your account, ask support for help. Do not assume a new account can inherit your previous content or records.

title: Dashboard and workspaces
text: Use Discover to find learning, My Learning Library to return to lessons and Publishing Workspace to create or manage your own content. Choose the area for your task Wistudi separates exploring, learning and publishing in the navigation. These are different views of your work, so a lesson you are taking and a lesson you are editing may appear in different places. Discover: explore available XP Videos and Flows. My Learning Library: return to video and Flow lessons associated with your learning. My Progress: view the learning progress available for your account. Publishing Workspace: find the XP Videos and Flows areas for creating, editing and managing your own content. My Profile and Account Settings: use the account menu for your profile and account preferences. Some navigation labels and options depend on the account and workspace you are using. A creator or administrator may see controls that a learner does not. Return to a lesson Sign in with the account you used when you started the lesson or received the invitation. Open My Learning Library and look for the lesson title. If you cannot find it, open the original invitation or assignment link. Follow the access message or the lesson's start or continue action. Do not use a creator's editing workspace as a shortcut to a learner assignment. The original invitation is the best starting point when you are unsure which content was shared with you. Find your publishing work For content you own or help manage, open the appropriate XP Videos or Flows area in Publishing Workspace . Check the title and content type before editing. If your account offers a workspace selector, check that the intended personal or organisation workspace is selected. A change of workspace can change the content and permissions you see. Do not create a duplicate lesson until you have checked the account and workspace. Understand locked navigation Some sections unlock through onboarding. The navigation can show requirements such as completing a profile, choosing learning preferences, or creating content. Expand the locked section and read its requirements. Use the action shown for the requirement you want to complete. Finish and save the requested setup, then return to the navigation. Completing onboarding does not grant organisation permissions or access to someone else's private content. If an access restriction remains, contact the person who invited you or support with the message you see.

title: Find and access learning
text: Open the original lesson link and follow its access instructions. A private link can have restrictions, and signing in does not automatically grant access to every lesson. Open a shared lesson or invitation Use the complete link supplied by your teacher, trainer or publisher. Check the title and creator on the invitation or content page. If asked, choose Sign In or create an account. Use the account intended for the invitation. After signing in or finishing account setup, return to the original link if the lesson has not reopened. Choose the start or continue action displayed and read the lesson instructions before beginning. If your teacher sent a replacement link, use that link rather than an older bookmark. Do not publish a private invitation link in a public group or on social media. Find learning without an invitation Use Discover to explore content available there. If you have already started a lesson, look in My Learning Library or return to its original link. Private or assigned content does not have to appear in Discover. If you cannot find a lesson in search, ask the person who shared it for the correct access link instead of looking for a similar title. Understand guest access Some shared experiences offer Continue as Guest ; others require sign-in. The choices shown depend on the content and its sharing settings. Guest progress can be limited to the browser session, and features such as saved account progress or reports may be unavailable. If the learning is an assignment or your teacher needs a recorded result, sign in with the intended account before starting. Do not assume work completed as a guest will transfer to your account later. A preview or guest view is not the same as being enrolled or having full learner access. Follow the invitation's instructions if it asks you to sign in. If the lesson will not open Sign-in required: sign in, then reopen the original invitation. Wrong account or workspace: check the signed-in email and the intended workspace where available. Invalid, expired or access-limit message: ask the sender to check the link and provide new access if appropriate. Repeated refreshing does not renew a link. Content unavailable: the publisher may need to check its publication or sharing settings. Ask them before assuming it is a device problem. Locked pages or activities: read the requirements shown in the lesson. Access to one page does not necessarily mean every page is open. If the issue continues, send support the content title, page link and exact message. Send private links only to the sender or support, and do not include passwords or reset links.

title: Troubleshooting
text: First record the error and protect unsaved work. Then check the account, link, connection and browser. Contact support with the affected page and the steps that reproduce the problem. Before refreshing or closing the page If you are writing a response or editing content, keep a copy of text you have not successfully saved or submitted. Check the save or submission message before leaving. Record the exact error, the content title and what you were doing when the problem occurred. A screenshot of the error is helpful, but crop or hide unrelated personal or learner information. Do not repeatedly confirm publishing, payment or submission actions while the result is unclear. Check whether the action completed first. If a credit balance or payment looks wrong, contact support with the transaction context rather than trying the same purchase again. A page or video will not load Check whether other pages load on the same connection. After protecting unsaved work, reload the affected page. Try the page in an updated browser. If needed, compare with another browser or a private window to check whether an extension or browser setting is involved. If only one video fails, note whether it is an external video and copy the exact player message. A source video can become unavailable independently of Wistudi. If the platform displays a desktop-only notice, use a desktop or laptop browser and reopen the original link. A private window may require you to sign in again. Do not clear browser storage or cookies as your first step: it can remove local session information and sign you out. A lesson is locked or progress looks wrong For an access message, check the original invitation and the account you are signed into. An expired link, access limit or permission restriction needs the sender or administrator to review it; changing browsers will not grant permission. If progress or a result appears missing, check that you are using the same account and the same lesson. Note whether you completed the work as a guest, in a preview or while signed in. Record the activity name, approximate completion time and any confirmation you saw. Do not restart an assessed activity just to test whether the record changes. Ask your teacher or support to review it if another attempt could affect your result. Saving or publishing did not finish Keep the page open while you check its status. Look for validation messages, required settings or a clear save confirmation. If the connection dropped, preserve unsaved text before retrying. If a publishing action appears to have used credits but did not complete, send the content title, approximate time and error to support. Do not delete the content to try to reverse the action; deletion is not a credit-restoration request. The Credit Usage Policy explains how verified technical errors are reviewed. Send a useful support report Email support@wistudi.com or use the support enquiry form . Include: Your account email and whether you were signed in or using guest access. The page link, content title and affected activity. What you expected, what happened, and the steps to reproduce it. The approximate date, time and timezone. Your device, browser and the exact error message. A screenshot if it helps explain the problem. Never send passwords, reset links, verification codes or full payment-card details. Share private content links only with the authorised sender or support.
